title: Cloud Boundary Pilot - Network & Residency Scoping
summary: Initial POC scoping for Peregrine Analytics pilot to run Redwood Private inside their AWS accounts. Primary concerns: strict data residency (region lock to us-east-2), egress prevention, network connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), and an agreed benchmark plan (20 rps sustained, p95 latency < 150ms for 512-token prompts). Next steps: share network template, run bench in staging with simulated prompt mix, and produce pricing/commit options for Dedicated+Private deployment.
next_steps: Redwood to share VPC peering and PrivateLink network templates and security checklist (Maya) - target 2026-03-09
Customer to provide sample prompt set and expected traffic profile (Marta/Connor) - target 2026-03-12
Schedule bench run with Redwood SE in customer staging (Darren + Marta) - target week of 2026-03-16
Security team to exchange SOC2/ISO certs and KMS architecture notes (Harpreet <> Ivy) - target 2026-03-10
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and pilot SOW (all) - 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC

Darren Patel: prepare benchmark harness and test scripts, include prompt mix generator by 2026-03-15

transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Darren Patel (Redwood SE), Ivy Ramos (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Peregrine CTO), Connor Blake (Head of Platform), Harpreet Singh (Security Architect), Marta Varela (SRE), Tom Briggs (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): customer wants private deployment in us-east-2, no egress allowed to other regions, options discussed: V P C peering vs Private Link, benchmarks for latency and throughput, security docs to be exchanged.

00:00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call from our side, I'm Maya, AE on the account. Darren's our SE, and Ivy from CSM.
00:00:12 - Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, hi Darren, thanks. I'm Lena, CTO at Peregrine. We'll get into why we need strict residency, but short story is regulatory controls for our financial data.
00:00:25 - Connor Blake: Connor here, heads platform, focus on network topology and how we keep traffic inside region.
00:00:32 - Harpreet Singh: Harpreet, security. Primary ask: no outbound egress to internet beyond our approved ranges, keys must stay in our KMS.
00:00:41 - Maya Chen: Totally understood. The objective for today is to land on a POC scope: connectivity option, bench plan, success criteria, and a timeline. We'll also map blockers like egress and KMS.
00:00:54 - Darren Patel: Quick technical note — Redwood Private can run with either VPC peering or PrivateLink for AWS. Peering gives lower latency, PrivateLink gives more controlled endpoint and no route table changes, but has NACL/SG differences.
00:01:10 - Marta Varela: Could you spell out the routing difference? We tend to avoid cross-account routes when possible.
00:01:15 - Darren Patel: Sure. With VPC peering, you create a route in the customer's route table pointing at Redwood's VPC — traffic flows directly, and you can avoid NAT for egress. PrivateLink exposes an ENI in your account via an interface endpoint; traffic goes to the service endpoint, and you control SGs per interface. Private link is spelled two words in some docs, sorry.. (laughter)
00:01:40 - Lena Ortiz: Our compliance team prefers PrivateLink historically because it's more auditable. Does Redwood support PrivateLink inside GovCloud or do we need a partner?
00:01:51 - Darren Patel: We support PrivateLink in commercial regions today; GovCloud is more nuanced. For our Private product we have runbooks for GovCloud but it may need an engineering enablement window. We can propose a timeline.
00:02:05 - Harpreet Singh: Key requirement: region lock to us-east-2. No token or request should be routed to other regions. Can you guarantee model weights and inference happen in us-east-2?
00:02:16 - Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin the model version and the deployment to a region. For the POC we recommend deploying Redwood Private stacks in your account within us-east-2 to ensure residency. We'll show the deployment manifest.
00:02:29 - Connor Blake: If we run it in our VPC, we'll need the network ranges and the ENI IPs for firewall allowlist. Also what about egress — we want to make sure there are no internet egress paths through the service.
00:02:41 - Ivy Ramos: We can provide a list of IP ranges used by the service endpoints and the expected ephemeral ports. For PrivateLink the traffic terminates inside your VPC, so outbound egress can still be controlled by your NAT/firewall.
00:02:55 - Lena Ortiz: For success criteria — we propose: 1) no cross-region egress, 2) p95 latency for 512-token prompts under 150ms, 3) sustained throughput at 20 RPS for a 1 hour run, 4) zero data retention on Redwood side beyond customer logs, and 5) KMS integration for key wrapping. Is that aligned?
00:03:18 - Darren Patel: That's a sensible list. Couple clarifications: the latency target depends heavily on model size and GPU shape. Are you planning to use a 7B style model or larger?
00:03:29 - Lena Ortiz: We're testing a 13B that we've validated for quality. We'll accept model recommendations if you think we should quantify with a proxy smaller model for the bench.
00:03:38 - Darren Patel: For 13B, p95=150ms at 512 tokens is aggressive but achievable on A100/A10G-class infra with right batching and no quant penalty. We'll include both a baseline and optimized config.
00:03:50 - Marta Varela: What's the typical token/sec per GPU for a 13B in your tests?
00:03:55 - Darren Patel: It depends — rough ballpark: 13B ~ 60-120 tokens/sec per device depending on sequence length and batch size. For the bench we'll run a simulated workload to reflect your prompts.
00:04:08 - Tom Briggs: On procurement: quick question, if we commit to a pilot Dedicated pool, how long before pricing and contract? We need to estimate budget cycles.
00:04:17 - Maya Chen: We'll provide a pilot pricing sheet and a two-tier option: short-term pilot credits vs reserved committed capacity for Dedicated. Expect the pilot quote within 3 business days after we get the sample prompt set and sizing.
00:04:30 - Lena Ortiz: Good. Let's circle back on benchmarks. What does Redwood normally measure? p50/p95, tail latency, tokens per second, and cost per 1k tokens?
00:04:41 - Darren Patel: Yes, we measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, and cost breakdown per token including network egress. For private deployments we'll also capture network egress rates and cross-account bytes.
00:04:54 - Lena Ortiz: Okay. For the POC we want a 60 minute sustained run at target throughput, plus a short burst test. Can you create the harness for that?
00:05:03 - Darren Patel: Yes. We'll provide a bench harness that uses your prompt set and simulates concurrency. It can run from a worker inside your account to remove network variability. We'll send the test plan.
00:05:12 - Harpreet Singh: On keys - we require CMEK KMS where the customer manages keys and Redwood never has plaintext access. Is that supported?
00:05:20 - Maya Chen: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for key wrapping in Private deployments. We'll share the KMS guidance and expected IAM roles.
00:05:30 - Connor Blake: Any certs we should expect? SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001?
00:05:34 - Ivy Ramos: We can share our SOC 2 and ISO docs. We'll also provide architecture notes and the security questionnaire template.
00:05:42 - Lena Ortiz: On network connectivity: which is simpler to operate for us? We prefer minimal route table changes.
00:05:49 - Darren Patel: PrivateLink is often operationally simpler and aligns with least privilege. VPC peering can be lower latency but requires route propagation. For strict egress controls, PrivateLink gives you more isolation because all traffic goes to the interface endpoint you control.
00:06:02 - Marta Varela: Does PrivateLink require public subnets? We don't want ENIs in public subnets.
00:06:08 - Darren Patel: No, you can place interface endpoints in private subnets. They create ENIs in your VPC in the subnets you choose.
00:06:15 - Tom Briggs: Are there additional AWS costs for PrivateLink we should account for?
00:06:19 - Maya Chen: Yes, PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint charges and data processing fees on AWS side. We'll include an example cost line item in the pricing sheet.
00:06:27 - Lena Ortiz: For the bench, we'll want to measure variance across 1 region deployment vs cross-region fallback. Can we simulate a failover?
00:06:36 - Darren Patel: We can simulate degraded capacity and measure tail latencies and failover time. Redwood's routing supports fallback to a different capacity pool, but for data residency tests we won't enable cross-region fallback unless explicitly part of the test.
00:06:49 - Harpreet Singh: We need an audit trail for requests — immutable logs with request IDs and timestamps for compliance. Is that available?
00:06:56 - Ivy Ramos: Yes, Private includes audit logs and request-level trace IDs. We can provide log retention options and export to your CloudWatch or S3.
00:07:06 - Lena Ortiz: Great. Timeline check — we'd like to get a bench run within two weeks. Is that realistic?
00:07:12 - Maya Chen: Yes, provided we get prompt set and networking details this week. So target bench run week of 2026-03-16.
00:07:20 - Connor Blake: We'll also need the allowlist ranges for the ENIs prior to bench. Can you provide approximate IPs or ranges?
00:07:26 - Darren Patel: For PrivateLink we'll provide service endpoint ARNs and a list of expected IP ranges; for peering we'll share the VPC CIDR we expect to peer with. These are in the network template.
00:07:36 - Marta Varela: How about data retention — you said zero retention by default? We need a written statement on retention policy for PII.
00:07:44 - Ivy Ramos: By default Redwood Private stores logs for operational reasons only, and you can opt-out of storing prompts. We'll provide a retention and processing statement in the security package.
00:07:55 - Lena Ortiz: If we're deploying in our VPC, who manages upgrades and patching?
00:07:59 - Darren Patel: For Private deployments inside your account, we provide an operator role and can run upgrades via an opt-in process. We'll coordinate maintenance windows with your SRE.
00:08:08 - Tom Briggs: For procurement — any minimum commitment for pilot infra?
00:08:11 - Maya Chen: Pilots are flexible; we often do a time-limited pilot with a refundable credit. Dedicated capacity has minimums. We'll outline options in the quote.
00:08:21 - Lena Ortiz: Ok let's quick nail down the success criteria doc so we can sign off internally. I'll repeat: region lock (us-east-2), p95<150ms for 512 tokens on 13B-ish model, 20 RPS sustained for 60 minutes, no egress, KMS CMEK, audit logs exported to our S3. Anything to add?
00:08:39 - Harpreet Singh: Add requirement: vulnerability scan or SCA report for the images used.
00:08:44 - Maya Chen: Noted, we'll include container scan and SBOM for the runtime images.
00:08:49 - Connor Blake: For bench variables — please include sequence-length distribution and concurrency in the plan.
00:08:54 - Darren Patel: We'll include a sampling of 50/30/20 short/medium/long prompts to mimic your profile and include p50/p95/p99 and GPU util.
00:09:05 - Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Anything else on the network side?
00:09:08 - Marta Varela: One more — we maintain an outbound proxy for egress. Will that interfere with PrivateLink?
00:09:13 - Darren Patel: If your proxy sits in-subnet as a forwarder, you'll need to ensure endpoint subnets can reach the proxy. PrivateLink itself doesn't force proxying, it's your network topology. We can test both proxy and non-proxy paths.
00:09:26 - Maya Chen: Recap of immediate deliverables: Maya to send network templates & security checklist; Darren to prepare bench harness and test scripts; Ivy to attach SOC2/ISO docs and security questionnaire; customer to send prompt set and traffic histogram.
00:09:42 - Tom Briggs: Sounds good. Procurement question: how will billing look during pilot? Upfront credit or monthly invoice?
00:09:48 - Maya Chen: Typically we do invoice with pilot credits applied, or a short-term committed invoice. We'll propose both options in the quote.
00:09:57 - Lena Ortiz: Let's aim to reconvene after the bench results. If the bench meets targets, we'll proceed to a 90-day pilot with a capacity reservation.
00:10:07 - Ivy Ramos: We'll tentatively block 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC for the results review.
00:10:12 - Lena Ortiz: Great. Any final questions?
00:10:15 - Harpreet Singh: One more security detail — who signs the DPA and do we need a subprocessing list?
00:10:21 - Maya Chen: We'll share the DPA template and subprocessor list; legal can start review in parallel.
00:10:27 - Connor Blake: Ok thanks — we'll send the prompt set by Friday.
00:10:30 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs.

(Transcription note: sections above include some auto-caption errors; product names sometimes split e.g., 'PrivateLink' -> 'Private Link', 'VPC' -> 'V P C', and 'KV cache' -> 'K V cache')

00:28:00 - [mid-call deeper tech dive, timestamps compressed in transcript]
00:28:10 - Darren Patel: on kernel selection — when we run 13B on A10G vs A100, kernel paths differ; we'll provide perf numbers.
00:34:45 - Marta Varela: can you show expected CPU/mem footprint for the sidecars?
00:34:50 - Darren Patel: sidecars are lightweight, usually <500MB RAM, but depends on batching queue settings.
00:40:12 - Harpreet Singh: We'll want encrypted logs at rest, is that supported?
00:40:17 - Ivy Ramos: yes, logs can be S3 encrypted with your KMS keys.
00:45:30 - Maya Chen: Final recap: send templates and security docs by 2026-03-09; customer to provide prompt set by 2026-03-12; bench week of 2026-03-16; results review 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
